ogTitle: Mercer Island Tile That Starts Below the Subfloor
ogDesc: Mid-century Island baths deserve straight answers about what's under them. Structure checked, membrane bonded, flood test photographed — then tile. From $14/sq ft. (425) 595-1079.

roles.heroLead: Under the original 4×4 tile, a sixty-year-old Mercer Island rambler keeps its secrets — and the tile was never doing the waterproofing anyway; that duty belongs to the membrane behind it. Our order of work: open the bath, report honestly on the subfloor, build the assembly, hold a photographed 24-hour flood test, and set tile last of all.
roles.trustCell: 12 years · family owned · based in Bellevue
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost on Mercer Island, WA?
roles.costP1: Mercer Island tile arrives at roughly $14–$26 per square foot, installed — the sum of tile, thinset and setting materials, substrate preparation and labor, where labor by itself enters at $11/sq ft. A tub-shower surround of standard scope starts near $3,200 and tops out around $6,800; a complete bathroom — floor, shower, niche — finishes anywhere from $6,500 up to $14,000. Mid-century houses hide their swing in substrate prep, so we look first and price after, never the reverse.
roles.costP2: File under counterintuitive: what shape the tile takes moves your bill further than what it costs. Install day can price a $4 mosaic sheet above $12 large-format porcelain, since the hours pool in cuts and grout lines while the tile receipt stays a footnote.
roles.costNote: August 2026 figures for Mercer Island, tile and materials and labor summed. Binding status belongs only to the written quote from the free on-site visit.
roles.layersLead: Seven layers from joists to grout. Every failed shower we open on the Island is missing at least one — nearly always the membrane, cut once to save a few hundred dollars, opened later at a five-figure cost.
roles.whyP1: A leak gives no warning. Water slips past grout, soaks into the substrate, and in a daylight rambler shows up a floor below — a ceiling stain in the rec room, a soft spot by the hallway — two years after the fact. The repair by then is framing, subfloor, drywall and the whole tile job again.
roles.whyP2: Waterproofing is about a tenth of what a shower costs. In a 1965 house it's also the difference between a remodel and a future excavation.
roles.scopeH2: What we tile on Mercer Island
roles.scopeIntro: Starting rates — format, layout complexity and, on the Island especially, substrate condition move them. The firm number gets written on site, free.
roles.cardShower: A shower is a system first — sloped base, bonded membrane, flood test on record — and only then a niche, a curb or curbless entry, and tile. The layer that vanishes is the layer you're buying.
roles.cardFloors: From bathrooms and kitchens to entries, mudrooms and lower-level slabs. First the subfloor is flattened — corrected outright if needed — then uncoupling membrane goes wherever movement or heat mats require.
roles.cardBacksplash: Subway, herringbone, mosaic sheet or slab-look porcelain. Outlet cuts tight, edges trimmed, grout picked against the counter rather than out of the box.
roles.cardHeated: Radiant electric mat on an uncoupling membrane, resistance verified before setting and again after, on a dedicated circuit. Only rational while the floor is already open.
roles.cardRepair: Cracked field tile, chalky grout, corners letting go. We measure, tap and tell you plainly: repairable, or substrate already past saving.
roles.cardDemo: Original tile, mud bed or backer out under sheeting and negative air, joists inspected while they're visible, debris hauled. Driveway left empty.

roles.faqH2: Tile installation FAQ — Mercer Island, WA
roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost on Mercer Island, WA?
roles.faqA1: Sum tile, setting supplies, substrate preparation and labor on Mercer Island and the result reads roughly $14 to $26 per square foot, installed; the labor component alone enters at $11 per square foot. A tub-shower surround starts near $3,200 and tops out around $6,800, while a complete bathroom — floor, shower and niche — finishes anywhere from $6,500 up to $14,000. The multiplier hiding in plain sight is format: mosaic sheets and large-format tile each demand notably more labor per square foot than ordinary 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower on Mercer Island?
roles.faqA2: On Mercer Island a standard alcove shower starts near $3,200 and tops out around $6,800, a figure that folds in demolition, bonded waterproofing, the sloped pan or base, tile, niche and grout. Benches, curbless thresholds, steam and full-height stone raise it — so does structural correction where a 1960s bath has seen water before. Call the waterproofing a tenth of the bill; it's the tenth that spares you the tens-of-thousands repair.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Yes — arguably it's the whole job. Under every shower goes a bonded waterproofing build: base sloped before membrane, membrane taken up the walls, corners, seams and pipe penetrations sealed, and then a 24-hour flood test recorded in photographs before tile is allowed on. Water moves through grout and tile freely; the membrane is what protects framing that has stayed dry here for sixty years and ought to keep doing so.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Give a Mercer Island bathroom four to six working days. The sequence: demolition under dust control, substrate work and waterproofing with its 24-hour flood test, a day or two of setting, then the closing pass of grout, silicone and trim. First use waits 24 hours while grout cures. Should demolition turn up subfloor repairs, you hear about it that same day, priced — never as an end-of-job surprise.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain for every floor and wet area: under 0.5% water absorption, denser and more chip-resistant than ceramic. Ceramic is a fair economy for walls and backsplashes. In mid-century Island baths we specify porcelain underfoot and in shower floors without exception, and let ceramic or glass argue for wall space.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes. Heated tile figures at $11 to $16 for each square foot installed, thermostat within the price — and over a crawlspace or daylight basement it's the least expensive cure a cold mid-century floor can get. The mat lies on uncoupling membrane, has resistance confirmed before setting and confirmed again after, and is fed from a dedicated circuit of its own. The window for it closes when the floor closes.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Usually, and on the Island especially. Removal and haul-away run about $3.50 per square foot, and demolition is the only honest look at a 60-year-old subfloor — rot, movement, past leaks — plus the only way to hold floor height at doorways. Tiling over existing tile on a flat, sound, bonded floor is possible, but it buries exactly the evidence we want to see.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost on Mercer Island?
roles.faqA8: Thirty square feet of Mercer Island kitchen backsplash goes in for $1,100–$2,200, with outlet cuts, trimmed edges and grout keyed to the counter as part of it. The premium end of that spread belongs to herringbone, mosaic sheets, framed range details and slab-look porcelain — what you're paying for is layout and cutting hours rather than fancier tile.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often, and we'll say when. Repair and regrout start at $8 per square foot — appropriate for stained or crumbling grout, a few cracked tiles from an impact, or corners needing silicone in place of grout. Hollow-sounding tile, a pattern of loosening, or a wall that flexes means the substrate is finished, and repairs only rent you time. We diagnose first, quote second.
roles.faqQ10: Which Mercer Island neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: The whole Island — Town Center, First Hill, East Seattle, Roanoke, Mercerdale, Mercerwood, Barnabie Point, Faben Point, Proctor Landing and The Lakes, North End to South End — plus Enatai, Beaux Arts Village, Newport Shores, Bellevue and Seattle over the bridges.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: A 2-year workmanship warranty stands behind our tile — carpet gets half that, because tile defects favor year two over week two. Where a manufacturer's bonded system goes in complete, the maker's own coverage applies alongside. And since your membrane and flood test were photographed, the record survives — small engineering history worth having when an Island house changes owners.
